top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: Attempting to change your notification settings for a specific channel would routinely fail. Not in an entertaining way, or the sort that teaches you something important on your way to greater heights. It just didn't do the thing it was designed to do. Sometimes misfortune carries with it no lesson. Anyway, it works again.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Notification settings never work properly

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Notifications were not being sent for huddles in DMs, which raises the question: How many people, in a definitional sense, are required to form a huddle? It's one of those philosophical quandaries like the Ship of Theseus or "How many geese make a gander?" No matter your answer, we argue that if a bug occurs but no one is around to report it, it still must be fixed.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) No connection on a huddle

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: When a message was deleted, it would very occasionally linger in the mobile app longer than was appropriate. See here, deleted messages: No lingering, loitering, dawdling, dithering or dallying. (Slack penal code 22.05.10)
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Keyboard always dissapears (impossible to write a message

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: Archived channels were erroneously appearing in the channel-specific notifications list, refusing to let the past stay in the past. "We're sorry, but the channel you're trying to reach is no longer in service" (though, you can always unarchive the channel if the time is ripe for a return).
top_matches.review: (reliability) No fix for annoying bug for days now. Enters wrong channel when tapping on channel name.

top_matches.release_note: (usability) Fixed: Uploading a new profile picture was sometimes failing, leaving people stuck with their old ones like an unfortunate driver's license photo. Contrary to popular belief, we've never aspired for Slack to feel like going to the DMV, so retake that photo to your heart's content.
top_matches.review: (reliability) Profile picture never updates on this app.

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) When using the TalkBack feature, some of our error messages were not being read out along with the field that triggered them. If an error message is written in Slack, but no one is able to hear it, does it exist? The answer is now a resoundingly audible "yes."
top_matches.review: (usability) Impossible to mark any message as 'read' - drives me crazy.

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) The mechanism governing the sending of audio clips was unsound, leading to failed uploads and stuck error messages. If you ever had to call an audible when audio didn't send, this fix is for you.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Huddles keep dropping and restarting poor audio

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Users trying to view a profile with the OOO status were out of luck when the app crashed on them. The whole experience was entirely out of line, and this bug is now out of the picture.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Keeps crashing when searching for contacts. Long delay in message sending status. Very bad experience

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Attempting to archive a channel shared in Slack Connect would return an unhelpful error. Incorrect, even. Maybe the real error was the errors we wrote along the way.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Not happy with the service should have a feature of storing the message like FB messenger. I have joined a channel and by mistake i have uninstal after that the messages I have sent to that channel's person that were removed.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: Links were not opening when Slack's preferences were set to hand off to an external browser app, instead providing a vague and unsatisfying error message. This has been fixed, and the only thing vague and unsatisfying now is the ending to that screenplay we've been working on.
top_matches.review: (reliability) Does not work anymore. Crash to home screen with no error / message.

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: If you posted a message to a thread, then long-pressed on that message and tapped "Send Reply to This Channel," nothing would happen. We are choosing to blame this lack of delivery on "supply chain issues."
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Constant issue with it not loading the newest message. Not marking message as read. Opening notification doesn't lead to the message I was notified about.

top_matches.release_note: (compatibility) Fixed: While browsing emoji or searching for people on an older version of Android, the back button would temporarily become ineffectual. This has been fixed, and if you're doing either of those things you can use the back button to hop back in time to where you were before. Look at you go!
top_matches.review: (compatibility) Doesn't support my version of Android.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: In larger group DMs, scheduling a message was triggering the "no backsies" clause, whereby the app would crash suddenly if you tried to make any changes from the Drafts & Sent screen. We appointed our amazing mobile engineers to be "it," and they went ahead and tagged out this bug.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) Slack not working on mobile data

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: For some people who have Slack set to a different language than their device, we incorrectly delivered a message about switching languages whenever they opened their Slack app. Our delivery owls have been retrained, so you should now only see that message when you manually change the language inside of Slack.
top_matches.review: (efficiency) There's huge delay in message receiption.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: Drafted messages within a given channel were sometimes overlapping with the message input placeholder text in other channels. Our staff physicists have concluded this was not, in fact, an instance of parallel universes colliding--it was just a good old-fashioned bug.
top_matches.review: (reliability) Filled with bugs that never get fixed. Fails to clear unread message flags randomly. When uploading an image anywhere, or sending a message when offline, the message will often glitch and her unfixable (can't resend, can't delete). These issues have been in the app for years and be they don't seem to have any interest it in fixing them. It's a real shame because the desktop app is great.

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: The app was crashing when scrolling backward in a channel, which was less than ideal (to put it mildly). Time may only move in one direction, but your channel history should always be available to you.
top_matches.review: (reliability) A bit bugy on mobile. Shows an error in a channel without a real error. Sometimes, there are problems with attachments on a mobile phone.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: On certain devices, tapping on a notification could lead to a weird state where backing out of a thread would always return you to that message from the notification you tapped. It was a phenomenon as confusing to witness as it is to explain, and we'll all be pleased to never have to experience it again.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) The /feedback command was broken, sending the bug report meant for Slack into whichever channel you happened to be viewing. It's now been fixed. /gif celebrate.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Tapping the search icon (magnifying glass) in a channel was sometimes causing the app to crash. We're ... pretty sure that's not what you were looking for. That said, if it's a bug fix you seek? Well, look no further.
top_matches.review: (reliability) Constant errors of "problem loading channel history".

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) When creating a new message, it wasn't possible to add multiple people to a DM (despite the checkboxes tantalizingly suggesting it was). We apologize for the mixed messages. Bug fixed? Check.

top_matches.release_note: (usability) Fixed: Beginning to edit your profile and then canceling those edits would sometimes cause the buttons at the top of the screen to render incorrectly. top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: Emoji reactions were sometimes failing to render as anything more than gray squares, which may have left you feeling slightly ... emotionless. top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: If you were someone with a whole bunch of workspaces, attempting to sign out of one of those workspaces was causing the app to freeze. Some people also reported hearing the faintest strains of "Hotel California" as the app refused to complete the sign-out. Now you may check out any time you like, and you can also leave.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: Tapping on a channel's bookmarked links would result in an error message that "Something went wrong." We hope that every time a link works henceforth, you will think to yourself, "Something went right."

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: In some rare cases, tapping "Threads" would show an error message instead of the threads you were looking for. We've sewn up that tear so your threads are once again where you expect them to be.

top_matches.release_note: (reliability) Fixed: Customized sidebar settings (sorting channels by recent activity, collapsing channel sections) were sometimes reverting to their defaults for no discernible rhyme or reason. Now that Halloween is over, we're done playing tricks.

bottom_matches.release_note: (cost) No big fixes to call out this week, but rest assured, there will be more in the future. Not that introducing bugs is our aim, of course. But missteps, adjustments, errors and corrections--these are the rhythms of life and the price of growth. We hope you're enjoying the ride, no matter where you happen to find yourself at present.
bottom_matches.review: (cost) Slack on Android is bug ridden and absolutely no replacement for Microsoft Teams, which has far more features and is bundled with Windows/365 free of charge. Nevertheless, Slack has its adherents, so on occasion has to be put up with, despite integrating with absolutely nothing. In summary, well beaten by Microsoft, Slack is a poor pointless cut down proprietary emulation of Teams, where Slack has to be paid for, if anything other than a rudimentary feature set. Best Avoided wherever possible.
